meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale, my son got a zero from software, and nobody called me first.
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. What do you have besides a machine's guess?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing that down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, so he pasted in a draft.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Then here's what doesn't move, Hale. Whatever comes of that record, nothing goes on his file and none of it happens in front of his class.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Turn the book. A seventeen-year-old misremembering a line is a mistake, not a crime.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay, I've read it. So what do you intend to do about the mark, Hale?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their thesis between an outline and an essay; that's what outlines are for. And you still haven't told me what you intend to do.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, and I'll hold you to every word of it in writing tonight. He'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Give me the date before I leave, Hale.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
He'll be there. Put the time and the room in your email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed that, under procedure 4.4, Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday the twelfth, not in front of his class and before December 1, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require that agreement in writing, with the time and the room for the rewrite. You said you would send it tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record; she still wants all of it in writing tonight with the time and room, and that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached well before her call.
What moved her: You turned the screen and showed the version history with its exact times, because it was dated, tied to Owen's own document and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Nothing; you owned the early zero in one sentence, never called Owen a liar and never leaned on the checker score.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, and Owen closed it; she never asked, and your version history, which put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, landed very close to that night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said students change their thesis between an outline and an essay, answer that point directly before you offer 4.4, so your third piece stands on its own instead of being left open.
